article.title: Garba Invitation Card in Gujarati: 6 Wordings You Can Print
article.excerpt: Six original Gujarati garba invitation card wordings, for a pol, a society, a home garbo, a party plot, an NRI hall and one person, each in Gujarati script with a romanised reading and English gloss, plus when to write આમંત્રણ or નિમંત્રણ.

keyTakeaways: A Gujarati garba card usually runs six lines: invocation, event name, a request to come (પધારશો), the date in Gujarati and English, the venue, and the host under નિમંત્રક.
Bhagavad Gomandal treats નિમંત્રણ as the respectful call to come, so it suits a home garbo; આમંત્રણ fits a society, party-plot or association card.
Opening invocations are a documented card habit: 68% of 50 Pakistani wedding cards and all 200 Iranian cards studied carried one.
48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so a forwarded card image must stay readable at phone size.
For one person, a single Gujarati line or the English-interface Be My Dandiya Partner page beats a printed card.

faqs.question: How do you say garba invitation in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: ગરબા આમંત્રણ (garba aamantran) is the general phrase for a society or event card. For a home garbo or sthapana, families write ગરબાનું નિમંત્રણ (garbanu nimantran), the more formal word for calling someone to a puja.

faqs.question: Should a Gujarati garba card say આમંત્રણ or નિમંત્રણ?
faqs.answer: Either is correct, because Bhagavad Gomandal lists નિમંત્રણ among the senses of આમંત્રણ. Use નિમંત્રણ for a family garbo or puja, where it carries respect and obligation, and આમંત્રણ for a society, party-plot or association event.

faqs.question: What does નિમંત્રક mean on an invitation card?
faqs.answer: નિમંત્રક (nimantrak) means the person or group who invites. Bhagavad Gomandal glosses it with the English word convener, so it is the right label for a society committee or a family name at the foot of the card.

faqs.question: Can I call a garba invitation a kankotri?
faqs.answer: Better not. Bhagavad Gomandal defines કંકોતરી as a kanku-sprinkled card for weddings and other auspicious occasions, and most Gujarati readers hear it as a wedding card. Call a garba card an આમંત્રણ પત્રિકા or simply આમંત્રણ.

faqs.question: What line goes at the top of a Gujarati garba invitation?
faqs.answer: A one-line invocation such as || જય અંબે ||, || શ્રી અંબે માતા પ્રસન્ન || or || જય માતાજી ||. We found no published sample of Gujarati garba cards to say which is most common, so choose by tone: Jay Ambe for a pol, Shri Ambe Mata prasanna for a society or family card.

faqs.question: How do I write the Navratri date on a Gujarati card?
faqs.answer: Write it twice: the Gujarati calendar name, such as આસો સુદ એકમ for the first night, and the English date. In 2026 the nine nights run Sunday 11 October to Monday 19 October; in 2027 they run 30 September to 8 October.

faqs.question: When is the Sharad Purnima garba night?
faqs.answer: In 2026 Gujarat plays garba again on the night of Sunday 25 October, Sharad Purnima, after Navratri ends on 19 October. If your society runs that extra night, print it as its own line on the card rather than folding it into the nine nights.

faqs.question: Is a WhatsApp image of the card enough, or should I print it?
faqs.answer: Print for a pol or society where elders without smartphones live, and forward the image to the group as well. SubhSandesh's own data shows 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so a card image has to stay readable at phone size.

faqs.question: How do I invite just one person to garba in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: One line is enough: આ નવરાત્રીમાં નવેય નોરતાં મારી સાથે ગરબે ઘૂમીશ? (Will you swirl through all nine nights of garba with me?). Send it on WhatsApp, or build it into a one-to-one page such as Be My Dandiya Partner.

faqs.question: Is the Be My Dandiya Partner page in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: No. Its buttons and labels are in English, though you type your own nine lines and note, so check the preview to see your Gujarati text before publishing. It invites one person only; it is the wrong tool for a society or family card.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Garba Invitation Card in Gujarati: 6 Wordings You Can Print

A garba invitation card in Gujarati usually runs six lines in a fixed order: an invocation (જય અંબે), the event name, a request to come (પધારશો), the date written the Gujarati way (આસો સુદ એકમ) beside the English one, the venue, and the host's name under નિમંત્રક. Below are six original wordings in Gujarati script, romanised and glossed in English: pol, society, home garbo, party plot, NRI hall and one person.

Two SubhSandesh measurements shape how to send it: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, which is where a forwarded card image gets read too, and in Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival we have measured (n=89, not Navratri data), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself. Late is normal; a card that is clear on a phone is the one that works.

## What does a Gujarati garba invitation card say?

A Gujarati garba invitation card is a short printed or forwarded notice that asks a household to come and play garba on stated nights, at a stated place, on behalf of a named host. It is closer to a notice than a letter: six to eight lines, no paragraphs.

That shape is a documented genre, not a Gujarati quirk. In [a study of 50 Pakistani Baraat wedding cards](https://gprjournal.com/article/genre-analysis-a-study-of-pakistani-wedding-invitation-cards) (Amjad and Riaz, 2020), an opening religious line appeared in 68% of cards and the inviters' names in 98%.

[A study of 200 Iranian wedding cards](https://www.academypublication.com/issues2/jltr/vol06/03/25.pdf) (Faramarzi et al., 2015) found an opening invoking God on all 200. Both studies looked at wedding cards from other cultures, so they show the pattern, not Gujarati usage.

## આમંત્રણ or નિમંત્રણ: which word goes on the card?

Both are correct, and the dictionary draws a line between them. The [Bhagavad Gomandal entry for નિમંત્રણ](http://www.bhagavadgomandal.com/index.php?action=dictionary&sitem=%E0%AA%A8%E0%AA%BF%E0%AA%AE%E0%AA%82%E0%AA%A4%E0%AB%8D%E0%AA%B0%E0%AA%A3&type=3&page=0) glosses it as a respectful welcome to come (આવવાને માટે આદરસત્કાર), adds that ignoring a નિમંત્રણ is a fault, and gives the older sense of આમંત્રણ as "please come again". Its આમંત્રણ entry lists નિમંત્રણ, તેડું and નોતરું among its senses, so the two overlap in everyday use.

In practice: use નિમંત્રણ on a home garbo or sthapana card, where you are calling family to a puja. Use આમંત્રણ on a society, party-plot or association card, which is a general call. The host's line is નિમંત્રક, which the same dictionary defines as "the one who invites" and glosses with the English word "convener", the right label for a committee.

One word to avoid: કંકોતરી. Bhagavad Gomandal defines it as a kanku-sprinkled card for weddings and other auspicious occasions, and Gujarati readers hear it as a wedding card first.

## Which invocation line goes at the top?

Put one short line, centred, above everything else. Three options fit a garba card:

- **|| જય અંબે ||** (Jay Ambe): "Victory to Mother Ambe". The shortest, and right for a pol.
- **|| શ્રી અંબે માતા પ્રસન્ન ||** (Shri Ambe Mata prasanna): "May Mother Ambe be gracious", a blessing on the event. Suits a society or family card.
- **|| જય માતાજી ||** (Jay Mataji): the everyday Gujarati greeting, warm for a home card.

We found no published sample of Gujarati garba cards, so how often each line appears on real cards is unknown. These are options built from the words' meanings, not a quoted tradition.

## 6 Gujarati garba invitation card wordings, by host

Each original wording gives the Gujarati card text, then a romanised reading, an English gloss and who it suits. Square brackets mark what you fill in.

### 1. Sheri or pol garba from the mahollo

> || જય અંબે ||\
> [પોળનું નામ] મહોલ્લા તરફથી શેરી ગરબા\
> આસો નવરાત્રીના નવેય નોરતે માતાજીના ગરબા ગાવા અને રમવા આપ સૌ પરિવાર સાથે પધારશો.\
> સ્થળ: [પોળનો ચોક], માતાજીના માંડવા પાસે | સમય: રાત્રે ૯:૦૦ પછી\
> નિમંત્રક: સમસ્ત [પોળ] રહેવાસીઓ

- **Romanised:** Aaso Navratrinā naveya norte Mātājīnā garbā gāvā ane ramvā āp sau parivār sāthe padhārsho. Nimantrak: samast [pol] rahevāsīo.
- **English:** Jay Ambe. Street garba from the [pol] neighbourhood. Please come with your family on all nine nights of Aaso Navratri to sing and play Mataji's garba, at the [chowk] by the mandvo, after 9 pm. Hosts: all residents of [pol].
- **Suits:** a lane where everyone knows the venue. Register: plain and collective.

### 2. Housing society garba from the committee

> || શ્રી અંબે માતા પ્રસન્ન ||\
> [સોસાયટીનું નામ] નવરાત્રી મહોત્સવ\
> સોસાયટીના સૌ સભ્યોને સહપરિવાર કોમન પ્લોટમાં ગરબા રમવા આમંત્રણ છે.\
> તારીખ: [૧૧ થી ૧૯ ઑક્ટોબર] | માતાજીની આરતી પછી ગરબા શરૂ થશે\
> બાળકોના નામ [તારીખ] સુધીમાં [નામ, ફ્લેટ નં.]ને આપવા વિનંતી.\
> નિમંત્રક: કારોબારી સમિતિ

- **Romanised:** Societynā sau sabhyone sahaparivār common plotmā garbā ramvā āmantran chhe. Mātājīnī ārtī pachhī garbā sharū thashe. Nimantrak: kārobārī samiti.
- **English:** All members and their families are invited to play garba in the common plot. Garba starts after Mataji's aarti. Please give children's names to [name, flat] by [date]. Hosts: the managing committee.
- **Suits:** a society notice board and its WhatsApp group. Register: formal આમંત્રણ, with the children's-names line as your RSVP.

### 3. Home garbo or sthapana for family

> || જય માતાજી ||\
> ગરબાનું નિમંત્રણ\
> આસો સુદ એકમે અમારે ઘેર માતાજીના ગરબાનું સ્થાપન થશે. નવરાત્રીમાં સાંજની આરતી અને ગરબામાં આપ સહપરિવાર પધારશો.\
> સ્થળ: [સરનામું] | સમય: સાંજે ૭:૩૦, આરતી પછી પ્રસાદ\
> નિમંત્રક: [અટક] પરિવાર

- **Romanised:** Garbānu nimantran. Aaso sud ekame amāre gher Mātājīnā garbānu sthāpan thashe. Navratrimā sānjnī ārtī ane garbāmā āp sahaparivār padhārsho.
- **English:** An invitation to our garbo. On Aaso sud ekam, Mataji's garbo will be installed at our home. Please come with your family for the evening aarti and garba. 7:30 pm, prasad after aarti.
- **Note:** garbo here means the pot itself: [Bhagavad Gomandal's ગરબો entry](http://www.bhagavadgomandal.com/index.php?action=dictionary&sitem=%E0%AA%97%E0%AA%B0%E0%AA%AC%E0%AB%8B&type=3&page=0) describes a perforated clay or metal pot with a lamp inside, kept at home for worship during Navratri.
- **Suits:** relatives and neighbours. Register: નિમંત્રણ.

### 4. Party-plot or ticketed garba night

> [આયોજક] પ્રસ્તુત કરે છે\
> નવરાત્રી રાસ-ગરબા મહોત્સવ\
> ગાયક: [કલાકાર] અને ગ્રુપ | સ્થળ: [પાર્ટી પ્લોટ], [વિસ્તાર]\
> પ્રવેશ ફક્ત પાસ સાથે | પરંપરાગત પોશાકમાં પધારવા વિનંતી\
> સંપર્ક: [ફોન]

- **Romanised:** Navratri rās-garbā mahotsav. Pravesh faqt pās sāthe. Paramparāgat poshākmā padhārvā vinantī.
- **English:** [Organiser] presents a Navratri raas-garba festival with [artist]. Entry with pass only. Please come in traditional dress.
- **Suits:** a party plot, which is a big-city format: [Akashvani's Gujarati service on 22 September 2025](https://newsonair.gov.in/gu/%e0%aa%ae%e0%aa%be-%e0%aa%85%e0%aa%82%e0%aa%ac%e0%aa%be%e0%aa%a8%e0%aa%be-%e0%aa%86%e0%aa%b0%e0%aa%be%e0%aa%a7%e0%aa%a8%e0%aa%a8%e0%aa%be-%e0%aa%aa%e0%aa%b0%e0%ab%8d%e0%aa%b5-%e0%aa%8f%e0%aa%b5/) named Ahmedabad, Surat and Vadodara.

No invocation line here; a commercial card reads better without one. Never print a price you have not fixed.

### 5. NRI association card, Gujarati and English

> || જય અંબે ||\
> [સંસ્થાનું નામ] આપને સહપરિવાર નવરાત્રી ગરબામાં પધારવા આમંત્રણ આપે છે.\
> [Association] invites you and your family to Navratri Garba.\
> સ્થળ / Venue: [hall, city] | તારીખ / Date: [date]\
> નિમંત્રક / Hosts: [committee]

- **Romanised:** [Sanstha] āpne sahaparivār Navratri garbāmā padhārvā āmantran āpe chhe.
- **Suits:** a hall abroad where elders read Gujarati and children read English.
- **Layout:** Gujarati first, English directly under it, English digits so nobody misreads the date.

### 6. One person: your garba partner

> આ નવરાત્રીમાં નવેય નોરતાં મારી સાથે ગરબે ઘૂમીશ?

- **Romanised:** Ā Navratrimā naveya nortā mārī sāthe garbe ghūmīsh?
- **English:** This Navratri, will you swirl through all nine nights of garba with me?

A printed card is wrong for one person. Send the line on WhatsApp, or build it as a page: [Be My Dandiya Partner](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) takes nine short lines (one per night) and up to six photos, needs no app or account to open, and ends in a 1080×1920 Dandiya Pass.

Its buttons and labels are in English, so type your Gujarati lines and check the preview before you publish. 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing; for a crush, that option is there.

## Printed card, WhatsApp text or a page: which format fits?

Four ways a Gujarati garba invitation travels are compared below. SubhSandesh's own numbers appear where they exist.

| Format | Who it reaches | Your own text | SubhSandesh measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Printed card (pol, society) | Every household, including elders without phones | 5–6 lines, wordings 1–3 | None: not a SubhSandesh format |
| Card image on WhatsApp | Group members with phones | Same 5–6 lines | None for images; 48.3% of SubhSandesh page views are on phones |
| Gujarati WhatsApp text | One chat or group | 1–2 lines, wording 6 | None |
| Be My Dandiya Partner page | One person | 9 lines, a note, up to 6 photos | 90.9% of started pages are published and shared |

Takeaway: print for the pol and the society, and forward the image to the group. Keep the page for the one person you want in the circle.

## How should the date, time and host lines be written?

Write the date twice: the Gujarati calendar name and the English date. Akashvani's 2025 report placed ghat sthapana at Ambaji on "આસો સુદ એકમ ના પ્રથમ નોરતે" (on the first norta, Aaso sud ekam), and that phrasing is what elders recognise.

For 2026 the nine nights run Sunday 11 October to Monday 19 October (રવિવાર, ૧૧ ઑક્ટોબર થી સોમવાર, ૧૯ ઑક્ટોબર). In 2027 they run 30 September to 8 October. Gujarat plays garba again on Sharad Purnima, Sunday 25 October 2026, so a society running that extra night should print it as a separate line.

Use Gujarati digits (૯:૦૦) on a Gujarati-only card and English digits on a bilingual one, never both in one line. For replies, add one line naming a person and a deadline.

## When a Gujarati card is the wrong choice

A Gujarati-only card is wasted on a society whose residents mostly read English. There, a bilingual card (wording 5) works better.

The Be My Dandiya Partner page has limits too: its nine lines go to one person, and its interface is English only. It does not sell garba passes, it cannot invite a whole society, and it will not find you a partner.

If the real plan is dinner after the last aarti, [a date invitation page](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) asks that question directly. An elder who does not use a smartphone should get the printed card in person.

auditReport.honestAssessment: The top 10 (US-served) has no page on garba cards in Gujarati at all: wedding-kankotri pages, onrender spam mirrors and a Notion stub, three of the top five unreachable. So this is the only result with six original Gujarati garba wordings, romanised and glossed, plus a dictionary-sourced આમંત્રણ/નિમંત્રણ/નિમંત્રક rule, which the meta title now names. The fix pass closed the paragraph and meta-title items but not the swap test: the genre evidence is still wedding-card research from Pakistan and Iran, and the invocation lines remain options of unknown prevalence because no corpus of real Gujarati garba cards was found. The domain has little authority for Gujarati-language queries, and low demand (autocomplete 6) is the ceiling; being the only on-topic page is the whole case for citation, not the writing.
